title: Put a quick-release toilet seat back on its two hinge posts and click both buttons
instruction: Put the toilet seat back on.
context: Janitors and cleaners (O*NET 37-2011.00; 2,172,500 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2023) take quick-release toilet seats off to clean the hinge area and put them back many times a shift. Both sockets have to go over their posts together and each must be pushed down until its button clicks; a seat that only rests on the posts lifts off when someone grabs it. The instruction says none of this.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the bench top. Bowl proxy: white block 43.5 (x) x 36 (y) x 2 cm, x -4 to 39.5, centred on y 0, its top is the rim. Hinge posts: chrome 1.2 x 1.2 x 2 cm at x 38, y +8 and -8 (16 cm apart), standing on the rim. Buttons: blue 1.2 x 1.2 x 0.6 cm caps on the posts, 30 g, top 3.6 cm above the rim, sprung up with 6 N preload (600 N/m), 12 mm travel; pressed 8.5 mm (about 11 N) one clicks and stays down at 10 mm. Seat: white rigid ring 38 x 34 x 2 cm, 1.0 kg (5 cm rails), hinged at its back edge to a grey 0.2 kg hinge piece that carries two socket housings (3.2 x 3.2 x 3.0 cm, 2.6 cm square bore 2.4 cm deep, open underneath) 16 cm apart; the ring swings up 0 to 100 deg about the hinge line. It lies flat on the rim with its back edge 4.5 cm forward of the posts (housings centred at x 33.5).
scoring: A socket is on its post when its bore is centred within 8 mm of the post and its bottom is under 16 mm above the rim (a socket resting on an unclicked button stands 12 mm up). It is clicked on when its button clicked under it (pressed 8.5 mm by the socket with the post in its bore) and it is still on its post. Score 0 if a gripper is within 2 cm of the seat or its hinge piece, a socket or a front corner of the seat moved faster than 1 cm/s over the last step, or the seat has fallen off the bench (latched). Otherwise 0.2 per socket on its post plus 0.3 per socket clicked on: one socket on 0.2, both on unclicked 0.4, one clicked with the other on its post 0.7, both clicked 1.0. The seat may be left down or up on its hinges. Scored at the last step; 1.0 held for 1 s ends the run.
reset_notes: Lift the seat off the posts (it is held once both buttons click; release by lifting the buttons' catch), let both buttons spring up, lower the seat ring flat on its hinge and lay it on the rim 4.5 cm forward of the posts.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; the seat is a square ring and the bowl a flat block. Sockets and posts collide as real geometry (7 mm clearance per side). Each button is a sprung slider; a click is a weld switched on once the socket has pressed it 8.5 mm, and the hinge piece is welded home once both have clicked (one clicked socket is not held down alone). The seat ring swings 0 to 100 deg on the hinge piece, so a fitted seat lifts on its hinges.
